Subject: Cedarbrook inference affordability recap & pilot scope

Hi Samira / Derek —

Thanks again for your time earlier. Quick recap from our call and the concrete next asks so we can get a pilot priced and scheduled. I kept this short and focused on the cost assumptions we discussed.

Key pain points you shared
- Token spend for customer-facing chat is already your #1 surprise line item (spiking during peak hours).
- Tight FY29 budget: the payments team has ~USD 150k allocated for model infra/third-party ML services. No large up-front commitments.
- Need for predictable latency (sub-300ms 95th on simple prompts) on account lookup and refund flows.

Goals we heard
- Reduce per-conversation token cost while preserving LLM accuracy for merchant dispute triage.
- Proposal: a 3-month pilot (ingest ~20k conversations/month) to validate batching + KV prefix caching and quantify unit economics.

High-level TCO assumptions (attached spreadsheet has line-by-line)
- Avg input tokens per call: 175; avg generated tokens: 220 (your sample set).
- Target throughput: 30 reqs/sec sustained, peak 90 reqs/sec (weekday spikes).
- Baseline hosted path using r-instruct-7b: estimated $0.045 per 1k tokens (hosted).
- With batching and prefix KV caching (expected 35–45% token reduction) + quantization to int8 on Dedicated or Private, modeled unit cost drops ~40–55% depending on hit rates.

Pilot economics (3 months) — ballpark
- Estimated hosted-only spend without optimizations: ~$98k for 3 months (tokens + inference).
- With the pilot stack (batching + caching + quantized serving): modeled spend ~$42–58k (range driven by cache hit rate).
- Implementation effort: 2-3 engineer-weeks from Cedarbrook (prompt templates, small routing integration). We can run the pilot on Redwood Dedicated reserve or in your VPC depending on security needs.

Open questions / asks for you
1) Confirm the sample token distribution we used (I attached the spreadsheet). If you can share a small export of 200 representative interactions we’ll re-run assumptions.
2) Is SOC 2 / encryption-at-rest a hard gating item for pilot infra? (you flagged compliance concerns)
3) Budget guardrail: is $150k the absolute ceiling for calendar year 2028 for inference services, or is there flexibility for a committed pilot with a discounted reserved capacity?

Next concrete steps
- We’ll update the cost model with your sample export and send a tightened 3-month SOW + pilot statement of work.
- Proposed date to sync on SOW: Tue, Jun 27 10:00–11:00 PT — does that work?

Attachments: cedarbrook_cost_model_v1.xlsx (cost rows + sensitivity tabs), redwood_pilot_sow_template_v2.docx

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick follow if anything above is off.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Ben — helpful summary. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Token assumptions: the 175/220 average looks right for the sample we shared earlier; I’ll upload a 200-row extract by EOD.
2) Budget: USD 150k is effectively a hard ceiling for public cloud spend unless there’s a clear committed-discount path. We may be able to move to a reserved spend if we can prove a 40%+ reduction in unit cost during the pilot.
3) Compliance: SOC 2 type II and customer-managed KMS are required for any private deployment. For a hosted pilot we’d need an explicit contract clause limiting data retention to 30 days and guaranteed region (us-west).

Two asks: 
- Can you add a sensitivity sheet showing a 25% and 50% cache hit scenario (I want to show this to procurement)?
- Please send any SOC2 artifacts and a sample data retention clause we can share with security.

Tue 10:00 PT works for me — booking now.

Appreciate the quick turn,
